question: Swami Vivekananda established which of the following social organisations in 1897?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramakrishna Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda established the **Ramakrishna Mission** on 1 May 1897.
 
• The organization was named after Swami Vivekananda's guru, **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**.
 
• The mission aims to work towards the welfare of the poor and the spiritual development of individuals.
 
• It combines spiritual practices with social service, promoting the teachings of Vedanta.
 
• Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission is located in **Belur Math, West Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda**:

 
 
• Born on 12 January 1863 as Narendranath Datta in Kolkata, India.
 
• Known for his speech at the Parliament of World Religions in Chicago in 1893, where he introduced Hinduism to the Western world.
 
• He was a key figure in the introduction of Indian philosophies of Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world.
 
 
 
• **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa**:
 
 
• Born on 18 February 1836 in Kamarpukur, West Bengal, India.
 
• A renowned mystic and spiritual leader, his teachings emphasized the universality of religions.
 
• He is regarded as an incarnation of God by his disciples, including Swami Vivekananda.
 
 
 
• **Vedanta**:
 
 
• One of the six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy.
 
• Focuses on the teachings found in the Upanishads, Brahma Sutras, and the Bhagavad Gita.
 
• Emphasizes the idea of Brahman (universal soul) and Atman (individual soul) as one.
 
 
 
• **Belur Math**:
 
 
• The headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission, established by Swami Vivekananda.
 
• Located on the west bank of the Hooghly River, near Kolkata, West Bengal.
 
• The Math is noted for its architecture, which fuses Hindu, Islamic, and Christian styles as a symbol of unity of all religions.
